title: The virtue missing from the deck

article.title: The virtue missing from the deck
article.lead: The Tarot deck has Justice, Strength and Temperance, but not the fourth of the old virtues — Prudence. In your matrix Justice appears three times. Strength sits in the point where you are easiest to pressure, in the strength of your family line and in the total of your chakras. Temperance is not on the scheme: it appears only when your two Chariots are added together. And the Hanged Man, whom people once tried to declare the card of prudence, is your mask and your spiritual purpose. Hence the main knot: a precise sense of measure that needs not one more proof of being right, but a well-chosen moment. How to find that moment is what this report is about. This is a symbolic reading for self-knowledge, not a forecast and not a psychological diagnosis.
summary: **Your main gift is a precise sense of measure.** You see an imbalance and an unfair deal before others do. The basis: Justice in the main talent, in the middle of the talent line and in the amplifier.

**On the outside you wait; inside you live by turns.** The basis: the mask is the Hanged Man, the centre is the Wheel. The Hanged Man also stands in your spiritual purpose, so a pause is your landmark for life. The cost, according to the book: self-sacrifice and difficulty saying “no”.

**Endurance is both your support and your weak spot.** Strength stands in the trigger point, in the strength of the family line and in the total of the chakras, and your thirties are its decade. The cost: not knowing how to rest.
**Your income grows where you explain and show yourself.** The Hierophant in the point of earnings coincides with your karmic task, and the Sun at the end of the money line asks to be seen.

**In closeness you need strong feeling, and it is easier to make peace with you through action.** The basis: the Devil at the entry to relationships, the Chariot in the point of reconciliation, the Sun in the dual point.

**Your family line leads a thread into every main area.** The nearest points of all four family lines coincide with your entry to money, your parents’ point, your dual and your centre — this happens for about one date in 860.
**Before forty your two main energies come one after another.** At 35 the age point is the Hierophant, at 37.5 it is Justice, and around 37–43 your personal purpose gives way to your social one.

chapters.h2: Scales, a pause and a sense of timing
chapters.conclusion: Your main gift is a precise sense of measure: you see an imbalance before others do. On the outside you look like someone who waits; inside you live by turns. What connects the two is the Wheel in the centre: it tells you when what you say will be heard, and then the pause becomes preparation for the right word.

cards.label: Main talent
cards.caption: Justice in the large circle at the top is a gift that shows from birth: seeing measure and a broken balance.

cards.label: Mask
cards.caption: The Hanged Man in the large circle on the left is how people see you: calm, restraint, the ability to wait.

blocks: If you read your matrix as a text, one word in it repeats more often than the others — **measure**. Justice appears on the scheme three times: in the point of the main talent (the large circle at the top), in the middle of the talent line and in the lower right corner. That corner is called the amplifier: it reinforces an energy that is present somewhere else in the matrix. In your case it reinforces the talent itself. Everything else is built around this axis.

formula.caption: **8 = 8 = 8.** One card in three roles. Your sense of justice is a working tool: it switches on by itself, and you use it every day, even when you say nothing.

blocks: In life it looks like this. At a shared table you are the first to notice that one person always pays while another “forgets their wallet” every time. At work you see that a task was estimated at two days when it holds five. In an argument between two friends you hear where each of them is half right. You don’t necessarily say it out loud, but you see it almost always and almost at once. The eight is the energy of people who understand how one event pulls another after it and who can dig down to the root of a problem.

On the outside this person looks different. In the point of the mask — the large circle on the left where the scheme begins — stands the Hanged Man. It is an image of a pause: a person who is in no hurry, who can wait and who looks at a situation from an unusual angle. People see calm and restraint in you, sometimes compliance. Meanwhile the scales are at work inside.

formula.caption: **12 = 12.** The Hanged Man stands both in the mask and in the spiritual purpose — for about one date in twenty. Lisovskaya writes that the spiritual purpose works together with the mask, the centre and the main talent and serves as a landmark all your life, long before sixty. For you a pause is a lifelong lesson.

blocks: The main argument of the matrix is between this pause and the centre. The centre holds the Wheel: a sense of timing, a love of movement, the ability to notice a turn before others do. The Chariot — speed and a goal — appears on the scheme twice, in the middle of the relationship line and in the children’s point, and once more in the calculated point of attitude to the material. Inside lives a person of movement. On the outside the Hanged Man teaches waiting. The energy of the centre does not always open up at full strength, especially when the mask holds a bigger energy (more on this in the findings), and in your case twelve is bigger than ten. So people around you see your pause more often than your inner pace, and you yourself sometimes take someone else’s “be patient” for your own decision.

The pair “I see unfairness — I keep quiet for a long time” is common. You have a third element added to it — the Wheel in the centre, a sense of timing — and it changes the advice. Speaking up sooner is only half the job. Your word sounds strongest at a turning point, when the situation changes by itself and a review looks natural. You notice such points before others do:

ul: **After a result.** A delivered project, a good week, a closed deal — the best day to talk about money and workload.
**At any change.** A new manager, a move, a change of season, a budget review — a moment when everyone revisits agreements, and your review will surprise no one.
**At the start of a cycle.** The first day of the month, the launch of a project, coming back from holiday — this is where a new rule is easiest to bring in.
**When the other person is calm,** and you have already cooled down.

blocks: The Hanged Man is responsible for weighing things up. The Wheel answers the question “when”. Use it as a tool: you noticed an imbalance — you wrote it down, weighed it and wait for the nearest turn. If there is no turn for more than a month, create one yourself: set a conversation for a specific date.

This argument has an old name. Ancient philosophers, and medieval theologians after them, named four cardinal virtues: Justice, Fortitude, Temperance and Prudence. Arthur Edward Waite, co-author of the best-known Tarot deck, noted that it has the first three, but — “owing to a curious omission” — it does not offer us any type of Prudence. People tried to find it. The eighteenth-century French scholar Court de Gébelin decided it was the Hanged Man; Waite replied that in this “he deceived himself”, and elsewhere listed what else the card had been wrongly called: “a card of martyrdom, a card of prudence, a card of the Great Work, a card of duty”. He himself saw a hint of the way of prudence in the Hermit, who walks alone by the light of his own lamp.

No deck has Prudence. What your date has is a set of cards from which it can be assembled. Justice — three times. Strength — in the trigger point, in the strength of the family line and in the total of the chakras. The Hanged Man — in the mask and in the purpose. The Hermit — in the total of the chakras and in the middles of both material family lines. The Wheel — in the centre. Prudence in the old sense is practical wisdom: knowing what to do and when. The Hanged Man’s pause gives you time to weigh things up; the Wheel finds the turn. A pause becomes martyrdom and duty only when it drags on with no end date.

formula.caption: **7 + 7 = 14.** Temperance is not on the scheme. Lisovskaya advises adding up repeated energies, and your two Chariots together give exactly that. Speed taken twice needs measure — in your case it is a skill that is built up.

blocks: This closes the last question of the image. The three virtues of the deck are present in you in different ways: Justice is given generously, Strength in excess and at a price, and Temperance is hidden in a sum of speeds. You don’t get it for free; you add it yourself — a pause before a dash, a budget before spending, the word “stop” at full speed.

formula.caption: **8 + 8 + 8 = 6.** The main talent, the middle of the talent line and the amplifier add up to 24, that is 6 — the Lovers, the energy of choice. The six is also your total of the earth, the material side of life before forty. In its plus it is confidence in your choice; in its minus it is hanging in the air without clear answers.

blocks: This sum explains why you need scales. Weighing for the sake of weighing turns into an endless “on the one hand, on the other hand”. The scales are there to choose: to say yes or no, to stay or to leave, to take or to refuse. When the choice is made, Justice is calm. When it hangs, she starts to judge — yourself, the people close to you, the past.

blocks.h3: Strength — the card of your thirties

formula.caption: **11 = 11 = 11.** Strength stands in the upper right corner, in the calculated strength of the family line and in the total energy of all seven chakras. All three coincidences at once occur for about one date in 260.

blocks: For any date the decade 30–40 stands on the upper right corner. Yours holds Strength, so your thirties pass under the same card as your family support and your overall reserve of energy. By the Golden Dawn correspondences Strength is also the card of your sign, Leo. There is one conclusion for these years: endurance is both your main resource and your main expense. How people catch you on it and how to protect yourself — in the findings.

ol: **Weigh.** Name the imbalance to yourself in words: who, what, how much, since when.
**Step back.** Look through the other person’s eyes: what do they see, what might you not know? This takes an hour or a day; a month is too long.
**Find the turn.** The nearest result, change or start of a cycle. No turn — set the date yourself.
**Say it.** Out loud, briefly, with facts and a suggestion of what to do next. No verdict and no lecture.
**Close it.** If you agreed, the question is out of your head. If you didn’t, decide what you do next and stop going back to the conversation.

blocks: Almost every area of life converges on this knot. In money, earnings stand where you explain the rules, and the entry to money is held by the Emperor, who needs a clear frame. In relationships the first thing you want is strong feeling, and it is easier to make peace with you through action. Each of the four family lines arrives at one of your main points. In 2026 and 2027 the year matrix puts Justice in the point of dealing with people. The next chapters show how the knot works in each area.
actions: Keep a “scales” note for a month: every time you see an imbalance, write one line — what, who, how much. After a month you will see what you keep quiet about most often.
Pick one imbalance from the note, find the nearest turning point — the end of a project, the start of a month, a change in the team — and set the conversation for it.
Before you say “never mind, I’ll wait”, ask yourself: am I choosing this pause, or was it chosen for me?

chapters.h2: What the automatic reading does not show
chapters.conclusion: Eight links that cannot be seen point by point. The main ones: your gift of measure is also a task of trust; rules taken to excess turn in you into control or protest; income grows where you explain without lecturing and stop hiding. Your endurance is both a support from your family line and the place where you get pressured, and the family line itself leads a thread into money, home, partnership and into you.
blocks: Below is what can be seen only by adding up distant points, comparing their roles or calculating points that are not on the scheme. Where a coincidence is rare, it says how often it occurs: the frequencies are counted over all dates since 1900 with the same calculation that builds your scheme.

finding.title: Your gift for seeing dishonesty is your theme of trust

formula.caption: **8 → 8 → 18.** The talent line repeats the 18-8-8 program (in the book the numbers are written from the other end).

text: You notice dishonesty before others do, and that is exactly why it hurts so much when you yourself are deceived: “how could I not see it?”. These two things are linked. Your talent line runs Justice → Justice → the Moon, and Yuliana Lisovskaya singles out this triple as a separate program — a scenario that repeats for many people. She describes it as a task of trust, honesty and understanding how one event pulls another after it. In her example the triple stands on the line of material karma; in yours, on the line of talent: the theme of trust is built into the gift itself.

The Moon at the end of the line adds sensitivity and imagination. You pick up on a trick from a tone of voice, but sometimes you fill in what was not there. Hence two imbalances: trusting too quickly those who speak beautifully about honesty, or checking everyone so hard that the people close to you feel they are being interrogated.

The book’s text on this program is harsh: deception and betrayal are described in it as lessons. For you it raises a question of choice. Your talent is more reliable when you yourself are transparent: you don’t promise too much and you name what your conclusion is based on. And when you tell two signals apart — “I find this unpleasant” and “this is unfair”. The first comes from the Moon, the second from Justice. The first is worth checking before you present it as the second.
finding.action: All next week, before every promise ask yourself: “will I really do this?” — and drop at least one you are not sure about.

finding.title: A calm mask dims a fast centre

formula.caption: **12 and 10.** The energy of the mask is bigger than the energy of the centre.

text: You often feel “it’s time” and still wait. Lisovskaya has an observation that explains this: “The energy in the centre does not always open up at full power, especially if the point of outer expression or of talent holds an energy bigger than it.” Your mask holds 12, your centre 10. She also writes that the mask leads a person away from their essence: through it they try to appear to others.

The Wheel in the centre is a person who feels good in motion and senses when it’s time. The Hanged Man in the mask is a person who waits. Your natural “now!” passes through the filter “I’ll wait, it’s awkward, not the right time”. On the horizontal between the mask and the centre stand two more cards: the Chariot in the children’s point and the Fool in the parents’ point — speed and lightness. Our reading: if home had a lot of freedom and little clear rhythm, you had to learn the pause yourself, as a way not to be swept up by someone else’s element. Check this against your own story.

The imbalance is easy to recognise: the moment has come, and you are waiting for permission, for a convenient occasion, for the other person to speak first. Then the moment passes and annoyance remains. When the centre is open, the pause is short: you stop to look and move on.
finding.action: Next time you feel “it’s time”, give yourself a day instead of a week: stop, look from the other side — and take the first step.

finding.title: Three Hierophants add up to the Devil

formula.caption: **5 + 5 + 5 = 15.** The Hierophant in the karmic task, in the physics of Anahata and in the point of earnings; the sum is the Devil, and it stands in the point where the karmic tail begins.

text: When there are too many rules, in you they turn into control or into a wish to do the opposite. The sum shows this. The Hierophant — rules, tradition, knowledge that is passed on — stands in your matrix three times: in the karmic task, in how you show love (the physics of Anahata) and in the middle of the money line, where earnings come from. Three fives add up to fifteen — the Devil, and the Devil stands in the point where the karmic tail and the relationship line begin.

The text on the karmic tail below tells in detail about the mirror kinship of the Hierophant and the Devil. Here something else matters more: in your case this kinship is not only in the tail but in the arithmetic of the whole scheme. A person who loves order and can explain how things should be done one day notices that they are behaving like a warden. Or that they are breaking with all their might a rule that was once imposed on them.

A scene: at home or at work you introduced a sensible rule — about the budget, about who does what, about deadlines. It was broken. The first reaction is to explain again, in more detail. The second is to check. The third is to stop following it yourself out of spite. The way out is to keep fewer rules than you would like, and to choose each one together with the people it concerns. A rule invented together needs neither guarding nor breaking.
finding.action: Count how many rules you keep in one important area — at home, at work or in your relationship. Cancel one you can live without and see what changes over a month.

finding.title: Earnings stand where the karmic task does — and the mask gets in their way

formula.caption: **5 = 5.** The point of profit and the point where the karmic tail ends are one Hierophant. This coincidence happens for about one date in twenty.

text: Money comes to you through what you stumble on, and its main obstacle is your own mask. Lisovskaya advises checking, when reading money, whether the energy of the money line repeats on the karmic tail: such a repeat links money and the life task directly. In your matrix the point of the biggest earnings and the karmic task are one card.

The Hierophant in the role of the task pulls you to hold on to the one right way. In the role of earnings it pays for what you can explain. Between these roles you have two more cards. The Hanged Man in the mask tells the market “I’ll wait”: the conversation about price is postponed until you feel entitled, and the mask grants that entitlement late. The Sun at the end of the money line demands the opposite — visibility: income grows when people know you by name, by result, by a talk you gave.

Hence an order of actions made for your scheme. First show a result — an analysis, a work sample, a talk, a client’s review. Then name the price. The Sun does for you what the mask cannot: it announces that you exist. A price after a visible result sounds like its continuation, and there is no longer any need to wait for permission. And the karmic task is passed along the way: the more willingly you show how you arrived at your method, the less “one right way” there is in it.
finding.action: Show someone one of your analyses or results — publicly or in person — and within a week after that name a price for similar work.

finding.title: The strength of your family line stands where you are pressured

formula.caption: **17 + 20 + 8 + 11 = 11.** The four corners of the scheme (their age marks are 70, 10, 50 and 30) give the strength of the family line — Strength. The same Strength stands in the upper right corner, on the trigger point. The coincidence occurs for about one date in seventeen.

text: The firmest support your family line gives you and your most vulnerable spot are one and the same card. The strength of the family line is not on the scheme: Lisovskaya calculates it as the sum of the four corners and calls it what the family line gives a person at full strength, “our direct talent”. In your case it is Strength: endurance, inner power, the ability to hold out when others give up.

The upper right corner, where the same Strength stands, is the trigger point: the energy through which a person is easiest to influence, and so the place where knowing how to protect yourself matters most. The hook phrase sounds like this: “You’re strong, you’ll manage.” You manage. And take on more.

In the minus of this energy is the habit of creating difficulties for yourself so as to overcome them bravely, and not knowing how to rest. Waite explains the Strength card without any “self-confidence”: in his picture a woman holds a lion with a chain of flowers, and that chain is, in his words, the light burden of a law once it has been taken into the heart. Strength is in its plus when you yourself decide what to carry and don’t take on other people’s loads to prove your endurance.
finding.action: Think up and write down in advance a phrase to say no with, for when you are asked to take on one more thing because you’ll manage. Say it at least once this month.

finding.title: It is easier to meet “your” person when you shine yourself

formula.caption: **19 = 19.** The Sun stands in the dual point and in the personal purpose — for about one date in fourteen.

text: The point where the lines of money and relationships meet describes a person who suits you energetically — in love, friendship, work. The personal purpose is what matters to live for yourself before forty. In both places you have the Sun. A repeat of the purpose’s energy on the scheme shows where it is lived out — in your case, in partnership and in money.

This turns the usual order upside down: “I’ll find my person, and things will get bright.” The Sun in the purpose is a task to become a source of warmth and clarity yourself: to make the complex understandable, to rejoice openly, not to wait to be noticed. A sunny person next to you is a reflection of that work. While your own sun is switched off, you are drawn to those who shine brightly but shine only for themselves, and next to them you are once again the one who waits.

The dual point also stands on the money line: a partner in the plus opens the flow, a partner in the minus blocks it — especially if a person dissolves in the couple and stops doing their own thing. For you the conclusion is practical: your own work and your own visibility are a condition both for money and for good relationships.
finding.action: Find one thing where you can shine yourself — speak, show a result, share what you know — and do it before the end of the month without waiting for an invitation.

finding.title: Speed is the common language of your money, your reconciliations and your attitude to children

formula.caption: **7 = 7 = 7.** The calculated point of attitude to the material (the material task 21 plus the entry to money 4: 25 → 7), the middle of the relationship line and the children’s point are one Chariot.

text: In money you want to achieve things quickly, in a quarrel to make peace sooner through action, with younger people to lead them forward. This is one card in three places. The line of material karma runs from the material task to the centre: the World, then the calculated point of attitude to the material, then the entry to money. The middle point, which is not on the scheme, describes your mood about money. Yours holds the Chariot — speed, a goal, a dash. You will find it in the middle of the relationship line too, which shows through what you can make peace with a person, and in the children’s point.

In money it is the wish to set a goal and dash for it; in the minus of the seven it is the habit of sacrificing your interests and wishes for the sake of the material. In reconciliation it is easier to come to terms with you through action than through talk: to go somewhere together, to do something, to rearrange things. In your attitude to children — your own, other people’s or children in general — it is the wish to develop them and move them forward.

The risk is substituting one thing for another: making peace with a purchase, curing a quarrel with a trip you cannot afford, hurrying a child or yourself towards a result because standing still is unbearable. The strength is the same speed directed at a clear goal and shared with another person.
finding.action: Try to end your next quarrel with an hour of doing something together — a walk, cooking, tidying up — and only after it go back to the conversation.

finding.title: Each family line leads into one of your main points

formula.caption: **17 + 11 = 10.** The point of the female material line nearest to the strength of the family line is the Wheel, your centre. Three more lines are built the same way.

text: Your family line does not stand apart from your personal life: each of the four family lines ends in one of your main points. From each corner of the scheme to the strength of the family line a line of three points is calculated; the one nearest to the strength of the family line is the place where the line of the family connects with you.

Here are the four connections. The spiritual male line (upper left corner) comes to the Emperor — your entry to money. The spiritual female line (upper right) comes to the Fool, your parents’ point. The material male line (lower right) comes to the Sun, your dual. The material female line (lower left) comes to the Wheel, your centre.

A coincidence with the dual occurs for half of all dates — that is how the calculation works. Each of the other three occurs for about one date in twenty. All four at once — for 54 dates out of 46 thousand since 1900, about one in 860.

Our reading: your family line passes a thread into every main area. The male line of values arrives in money — your attitude to responsibility and order in money probably comes from there. The female line of values arrives in the atmosphere of home, in lightness or the lack of it. The male line of deeds arrives in your choice of partner: which person feels like your own. The female line of deeds arrives in your very essence, in your sense of timing. So whatever you change in money, home, partnership or yourself, you also change the continuation of one of your family lines.
finding.action: Pick one of the four areas and ask your elders how the family treated exactly that — money, home, choosing a partner, change. Write down one rule you want to continue and one you will end with yourself.

chapters.h2: A pause outside, a turn inside
chapters.conclusion: You are seen as a calm and patient person who is in no hurry to draw conclusions. Inside you sense change quickly and know exactly where things are unfair. The strength of this make-up is that you are rarely wrong about people or about the moment; the cost is work nobody sees and a strictness with yourself that you would never allow anyone else.

cards.label: Mask
cards.caption: The Hanged Man is what people read first: restraint, absorption, a look from an unusual angle.

cards.label: Centre
cards.caption: The Wheel in the centre is your essence: a sense of timing, movement, the ability to catch a turn.

blocks: People see in you a calm person who listens more than talks and is in no hurry to agree. This is the mask — the Hanged Man in the large circle on the left: what is read about you first and what you yourself look at the world through. Waite stressed three details in his drawing of this card: the tree is living wood, with leaves; the face expresses deep entrancement, not suffering; it is life in suspension, but life. That is often how you are seen: a person within themselves, calm, a little detached.

A scene at work. A new plan is being discussed. Everyone has spoken in five minutes; you are silent: you need to see the whole picture, to look at how it works for the department, for the client, for whoever will do it. Colleagues decide you have no opinion or you agree. An hour later you say two sentences after which the plan is rewritten. It surprises people every time, though there is nothing to be surprised about: you waited until the whole picture came together.

This mask has a side that people don’t usually expect from someone “patient”: the ability to say “no”, to know your worth, to sense time and arrive on time. The reverse side is self-sacrifice, difficulty refusing, impostor feelings, a habit of being late. A pause after which you say “no” works for you. A pause after which you agree against your will works against you.

Inside you are a person of flow: quick to get going, with good intuition, you sense an opportunity and don’t miss it. This is the centre — the Wheel, your essence and where you draw energy from. In an even week with no news you get bored; when something shifts — a new offer, a move, an unexpected conversation — energy appears. You understand before others that a situation is turning, and inwardly you are already ready.

The minus of this energy is anxiety, suggestibility and living in cycles, when the same mistakes repeat round and round. For you it is linked to the mask: if the pause becomes a habit, the Wheel spins idle — you sense the turn but don’t take it, and the next turn brings the same annoyance.

In a calm state you have two modes and switch between them. This can be seen from the four inner points around the centre. On the left is the Fool, the parents’ point. At the top is the Moon, the additional talent. On the right is the Emperor, the entry to money. At the bottom is the Devil, what you want from relationships. The left and top points are fluid: freedom, lightness, starting from a blank page, sensitivity, living by feel. The right and bottom points hold: order, rules, control, strong desire, grip.

Our reading of such a square: when tired, you either let everything go — “to hell with it, I’ll start over” — or clamp down — new rules, control, a schedule. The Wheel in the centre is the switching mechanism itself. Prudence here means noticing which mode the moment needs. A quarrel with someone close asks you to let go. Chaos in money asks you to take hold. It is easy to mix them up: to clamp down on the relationship and let go of the budget.

blocks.h3: Why it is easy to load you up

blocks: The Hanged Man’s mask tells the world: this person can wait. Strength on the trigger point answers pressure with endurance. Together they create the image of a person who is convenient to rely on and convenient to load up: from the outside it seems you will both endure and wait. So you get more than others of other people’s unfinished work, postponed promises and requests to be patient a little longer. Protection takes a skill, and strength won’t help here: talk about your limits before you are asked about them. “I’m not taking new tasks this week” sounds calm, and that is exactly why it works.

The strong side of this make-up is precision. You are rarely wrong about people: the calm mask gives you time to look at a person closely, the Moon in the talent hears the tone, Justice weighs the actions. In a crisis you don’t panic out loud. People trust you because you don’t throw words around, and when you say “this is unfair”, they listen.

The cost is strictness with yourself. The Justice you apply so precisely to others you apply to yourself with no discounts, and the Hanged Man’s mask adds the doubt “do I have the right”. A scene: at work you made a small mistake — mixed up a date in an email. A colleague forgot about it in an hour, your manager didn’t notice. You come back to that mistake for a week, double-check every next email and in the end don’t take a task you were interested in — “what if it happens again”. A simple check helps: would you say the same thing to a friend in the same situation? If not, you are judging yourself by a different law, and that law is worth revising.
actions: In three conversations this week say what you think in the first ten minutes, even briefly: “this is my view for now, I may change my mind”.
Next time you start picking apart your own mistake, ask: “what would I tell a friend?” — and tell it to yourself.
In the evening note one situation from the day: did you let it go or clamp down — and which mode was really needed?

chapters.h2: Talents and work: untangling disputes and explaining decisions
chapters.conclusion: You are strongest where a disputed situation between people has to be untangled and a decision explained so that people can use it. Work with clear criteria and the right to your own conclusion suits you. You fade where rules are changed silently and you have to wait with no end date.

cards.label: Main talent
cards.caption: Justice at the top is a gift that switches on by itself: seeing measure and naming an imbalance.

cards.label: Inner point of talent
cards.caption: The Moon at the end of the line is sensitivity, imagination, the ability to hear what is left unsaid.

blocks.h3: The talent line as a whole

blocks: You have seen measure since childhood, and it can also be learned as a craft. The talent line runs from the top to the centre: Justice, Justice again, the Moon. The first point is a talent that shows by itself. The other two are additional: on their own they rarely open up, but they develop easily if you give them attention. The result is a rare combination: the same Justice is both innate and worth training. You already see an imbalance, and with training you will be able to do it professionally — with a method, criteria and arguments.

The Moon at the end of the line changes the character of this precision. Your precision begins with people: first you hear where a person is hurting or awkward, and only then do you lay the situation out piece by piece. The eighteenth energy is a rich inner world, a good memory, an ability to understand people and to write. Its minus is fears and pictures a person fills in by themselves. So at work it is especially important for you to tell an impression from a conclusion: you get the impression in a minute, the conclusion after talking to both sides.

ul: Untangle disputed situations: who is right, about what and how far — so that both sides accept the analysis as fair.
Find the weak spot in a contract, plan, estimate or text — where what was declared differs from what was done.
Hear what a person is not saying and ask in a way that makes it easier for them to say it.
Turn chaos into a clear order — an instruction, a sequence of steps, a checklist. Here the Hierophant in your point of earnings and the Emperor at the entry to money are at work.
Explain a complex rule through the living example of a particular person: the Moon finds the example, the Hierophant makes a rule of it.

head: Field
What in it is yours
rows: weighing both sides’ arguments, hearing what is unsaid and explaining the decision
Advising on rules: labour, family, consumer
translating a law or regulation into the language of a specific situation
Methodology and training within your profession
gathering experience into a rule that others will start to use
People management: evaluation, complaint handling, fair procedures
making sure the rules are the same for everyone and explaining decisions
seeing where figures or processes differ from what was declared
hearing where a text is wrong and proving it with a source
depth, patience and a nose for motive

blocks: The fields in the table rely on different cards of yours, and that decides how fully you will open up in them. The first four hold on to the whole bundle at once: Justice weighs, the Moon hears people, the Hierophant in the point of earnings explains the decision and turns it into a rule. If you are choosing your main work, choose from here — especially where living people argue and where the decision then has to be explained. Audit, control and checking figures rely mainly on Justice: you will be precise there, but without people and without explaining you will quickly get bored. Psychology and research rest more on the Moon and are good as a second role: your main work needs a conclusion that can be defended.

Your best format is deep work alone, then a finished conclusion on the table. The Hanged Man gives time to look at a task from all sides, Justice to formulate a result that can be defended. Projects with a clear finish work well: the Wheel in the centre and the Chariot in two points love movement, and endless processes dim them. Roles that suit you are those of someone who checks, makes the decision, consults in sessions, writes the conclusion.

You are stronger in an environment where criteria are named in advance, where you can say “this isn’t ready yet” or “I disagree” without being punished, where quality is valued above haste and where the manager explains their decisions. A new direction, a change of tasks, a project move charge you up rather than scare you.

You fade where rules are changed silently; where loyalty is valued above truth; where “we’ll discuss it later” drags on for months; where work is judged by mood; where you carry someone else’s area because you’ll manage. Each of these places hits one of your main points: Justice, the Hierophant, the pause-mask, Strength on the trigger.

blocks.h3: How to check a job or a project

blocks: Before agreeing to a new position, client or big project, go through six questions. The more “yes” answers, the more room this work has for your talent.

ol: Is there a moment here when things have to be weighed and a clear conclusion given?
Are the criteria by which the result will be judged named before the work starts?
Can I say “I disagree” and be heard?
Will there be movement: stages, a finish, new tasks?
Is it clear who is responsible for what and who pays for a mistake?
Can I explain and teach others here — and be paid for it separately?

blocks: You are inspired by summing up: closing a big stage and seeing what came of it; gathering scattered pieces into one picture; sorting through an archive, a family history, accumulated data; hearing “we need you specifically”. This is the upper left corner — the point of inspiration, and yours holds Judgement: the energy of summing up, of a large volume of information and of memory. The same point shows what takes your strength away: labels and judgements from others and stages left hanging unfinished.
actions: Write out three tasks from the past year after which you felt “this is mine”. Find what they have in common: almost certainly it involved untangling a dispute or explaining a rule.
Take one task where you can give a written conclusion with arguments — an analysis, an expert opinion, a review — and do it as an expert assessment: criteria, facts, conclusion, what to do next.
Once every three months hold a “summing up” for yourself: what is finished, what is weighed, what I am letting go. For you this is a source of strength.

chapters.h2: Money: order, visibility and the courage of scale
chapters.conclusion: Money comes to you through responsibility for order and through explanation that helps people. It is held back by control for the sake of control, by waiting for your worth to be noticed on its own, and by the fear of moving to a bigger scale. After forty your main resource is passing on experience beyond one circle of people.

cards.label: Entry to money
cards.caption: The Emperor is both the entry and the block: money opens through responsibility and order and closes through rigidity.

cards.label: Profit and earnings
cards.caption: The Hierophant in the middle of the money line: you are paid for what you can explain and turn into a rule.

blocks.h3: Where money comes from and what holds it

blocks: Money comes to you when you take on the structure: you are responsible for an area, set up a process, keep deadlines for others. This is the entry to money — the Emperor in the inner circle to the right of the centre. Lisovskaya describes this point as an entry and a block at the same time: the energy on it “is in the minus, but at the same time opens the financial flow”, so a person’s money can swing up and down. The Emperor’s block is rigidity, excessive control, the wish to hold everything yourself. An Emperor who holds everything alone gets tired and stops taking on anything new.

The biggest earnings come through explanation: the middle of your money line is the Hierophant. A five in this point means education, public speaking, work with documents, finance and rules. As the findings say, the same card is your karmic task, and what hinders it most is the mask that waits for permission to name a price.

At the end of the money line, where it meets relationships, stands the Sun. In the money sense this point shows the beliefs that get in the way of earning. The Sun’s minus as a belief is self-reproach, workaholism and the habit of treating any failure as a disaster. Together the Emperor and the Sun make a clear knot: you want to control the result and to be visible, but not before everything is flawless. While it isn’t flawless, you work a lot and quietly.

blocks.h3: Material karma: the theme of scale

formula.caption: **21 → 7 → 4.** The line of material karma: the World sets the theme, the calculated Chariot (21 + 4 = 25 → 7) shows your mood about money, the Emperor is the entry.

blocks: In material matters you can do more than you allow yourself. The main point of the line is the World: scale, freedom from borders, other cities and countries, languages, big projects. In its minus — closedness, categorical thinking and a fear of expanding. This line is lived from birth mostly in the minus, and the task is to notice how its energies work in you and to bring them into the plus.

What this can look like: you are able to run your work a level higher than you do now, but you choose a familiar circle of clients, your own city, one source of income. The Chariot in the attitude to the material adds impatience: you want a result fast, and if it hasn’t come in a month, it seems it never will. The Emperor at the entry squeezes all of this into a frame. The plus of the same line is a person who can set a big goal, move towards it fast and build the order on which the result rests.

blocks.h3: Money scenarios — check which one is yours

blocks: These are hypotheses drawn from combinations of cards. If you recognise yourself, there is something to work with.

ul: **“A fair share.”** You count who put in how much, and to keep things fair you take on more: you pay for shared things, finish other people’s work, don’t send an invoice for small things. In total your share turns out smaller than anyone’s. The basis: Justice three times and Strength on the trigger.

**“I’ll wait until they offer.”** You know you work better than others, but you don’t ask for a raise and don’t raise your price — you wait to be noticed. The Hanged Man’s mask tells the world “I don’t mind waiting”, and the world agrees. Among the advice for the twelfth energy there is a direct one: learn to take money for your work.

**“Dash and brake.”** First a decisive purchase or investment for a big goal — a course, a move, equipment. Then hard saving and guilt. Then another dash. The basis: the Chariot in the attitude to the material, the Emperor at the entry and the Wheel in the centre, which in its minus lives in cycles.

**“Money through the partner.”** Your finances change noticeably along with the person close to you: next to one they open up, next to another they shrink. The dual point stands on the money line and affects earnings both ways.
**Free work “out of conscience”.** Finishing for someone else, staying an extra hour, advising “as a friend”. Each small thing is fair; together they add up to unsold work.
**A dash with no road.** A purchase or investment for a big goal that has no plan and no deadline. The Chariot spends fast, and then the Emperor punishes with saving.
**Money instead of a conversation.** Buying a present after a quarrel, paying for a trip to ease the tension. Peace through action works; peace through a purchase lasts until next time.

**Long disputes about fairness.** Time and energy spent proving you are right on a matter worth less than the dispute itself. Before any showdown it helps to ask: what is winning worth, and what is the time it takes?

blocks: Your decade 40–50 runs under the World — the same card that stands in your material task. The theme of scale, which before forty sounded like the question “will I dare”, becomes the theme of the period itself. At the same time your personal purpose gives way to your social one, and this period is the time to pass accumulated experience on to others. Your social purpose is Judgement: gather what was done and pass it on. Inside the decade the age points run like this: at 42.5 — the Hierophant again, at 45 — Strength, at 47.5 — the Sun.

For money this means: knowledge gathered before forty is worth more after forty if it goes beyond one circle — another audience, another country, a format that doesn’t need your presence every minute. You can prepare for this in advance: write down how you do what you do well, collect examples, try small steps beyond the usual borders. The transition is gradual, over several years before and after forty.

ul: **Your own share comes first.** Before dividing “by conscience”, write down what your contribution is worth at market rates.
**Visible result first, price second.** The Sun at the end of the line opens what the mask keeps closed.
**Money and relationships are separate conversations.** A money question is not settled in the middle of making up, and making up is not bought.
**Review your price at a turning point.** After a good result, at the start of a year or a new project, the Wheel helps you, and a review looks natural.
**One big goal a year — with a budget and a deadline.** The Chariot’s dash is useful when it has a road.

actions: Count how much work you did for free over the past month because it felt fairer. Name the amount the market would have put on it.
Show one of your results to people who might find it useful, and after that offer them similar work at a named price.
Choose one step beyond your usual borders for the next three months — a new audience, an online format, another city — and write it down with a date.

chapters.h2: Relationships: strong feeling and peace through action
chapters.conclusion: In closeness you want strength and authenticity: a feeling that sweeps you up and a person you are never bored with. It is easier to make peace with you through doing something together than through a long analysis. “Your” person is warm, generous and bright in their own right. The main risk is a silent tally of grievances; the way out is to name an imbalance within a day and to invent rules together.

cards.label: What you want from relationships
cards.caption: The Devil in the inner circle below the centre — passion, intensity, grip; the karmic tail also begins here.

cards.label: Dual
cards.caption: The Sun on the lower right diagonal — the energy of the person who suits you best.

blocks: Your way of being with people is the same in love, friendship and work: first a strong wish for real contact, then getting closer through a shared task, and finally warmth. These are the three points of the relationship line: the Devil, the Chariot, the Sun.

**You want the real thing.** The first point of the line is what you look for in people and how you look at them. Yours holds the Devil: passion, brightness, quality, the ability to captivate. You don’t need warm but limp relationships — you want them to be real, with tension and strength. The same point starts the karmic tail, so its minus switches on easily: dependence, obsession, the wish to get your way at any price. The advice of this energy is to lower your demands on yourself and others and not to slip into idealisation. The risk for you is confusing intensity with tests: “if they love me, they’ll take it”.

**You get close in motion.** The second point is how you show yourself to others and through what people can make peace with you. Yours holds the Chariot. This point is worth reading together with the mask, and in your case they argue. The Hanged Man’s mask keeps a distance: you look closely and don’t open up at once. The Chariot gets close through doing: a shared project, a trip, sport, a move, a renovation. So people become close to you when you do something together, and long talks “about us” are more likely to push you apart.

**A sunny person suits you.** The third point is the dual, the energy of a person who understands you almost without words. Yours holds the Sun, which is also your personal purpose — more on this in the findings.

blocks.h3: What you bring to a relationship

blocks: Before talking about difficulties, it is worth naming what the person next to you gets. Honesty: with you there is no need to guess where the truth is, if you have said it. Depth: the Moon in the talent hears what is going on with the other person before they understand it themselves. Faithfulness to your word and to rituals: the Hierophant in the physics of Anahata makes love reliable. Movement: with you a relationship doesn’t stagnate, there is always a shared task, a trip, a plan. And a strength of feeling that cannot be mistaken for polite interest.

ul: Warm and generous: shares attention, time and money without counting — and next to them your Justice has nothing to recount.
Bright in their own right: they have their own work, their own interests and their own light, and don’t need to live your life.
With a good sense of humour and no habit of despair: for them a failure is an episode.
Caring, loves children and people, comes to help without being asked.
The minus of the same energy is domineering, categorical behaviour, pressure and self-reproach. The Sun that warms and the Sun that burns are one card; watch how a person behaves when they are tired.

blocks: How to check this in practice. Lisovskaya advises looking for your dual energy in the other person’s matrix: in the centre, the mask, the main talent, the spiritual purpose, or in the first and last points of their relationship line. If the Sun stands there, understanding will be almost intuitive. If the person has it on the trigger, in material karma or in the karmic tail, the energy is shared but painful for them, and there will be misunderstandings. With a person who has the Devil in the same places you have a lot in common and a few topics where you speak different languages. A relationship can be built with any energies; this is a landmark, and the decision stays with you.

blocks.h3: The main risk: a silent tally

blocks: A scene. Someone close promised to deal with a shared matter — call about the renovation, renew the joint insurance, sort out the documents. They didn’t. You made a mental note and said nothing: it felt awkward to remind them. The second time — another note. The third time you did everything yourself and felt you were right. The tally grows. The wish for strength and authenticity that stands at the entry to your relationships quietly turns into control: you check, notice, compare. The person next to you feels the cold but doesn’t understand where it comes from.

Then the turn comes. The Wheel in the centre makes it sharp: one day you announce a decision — “I can’t go on like this” — which for you is the result of months of weighing and for the other person a bolt from the blue. On your side everything was fair. On theirs there was never a single conversation.
Hence a rule worth remembering: **the truth said within a day is a conversation. The truth said six months later is already a verdict, even if the words are the same.**

ul: **A short check-in once a week.** Fifteen minutes, two questions: what felt unfair this week and what was good. Justice gets an outlet while the tally is small.
**Rules made together.** Who is responsible for what, how you split money, what you do when one of you can’t keep up. A rule you invented alone, the other person will take as an order.
**A pause with a deadline.** When you need to think, say: “I need time until this evening.” The Hanged Man needs a pause; the other person needs to know when it will end.
**Make peace through action.** After a quarrel there is no need to analyse everything at once. First do something together, then talk — that is how your point of reconciliation works.
**The right to be imperfect.** Don’t test love with trials. Strength of feeling rests on freedom.

blocks: If you are not in a couple right now, the same line suggests where to meet people: where people do something together — hikes, volunteering, courses, shared projects. The Chariot recognises its own in motion, and the mask has time to look closely while the hands are busy.
actions: Agree with someone close on a weekly fifteen-minute check-in and hold the first one this week.
Recall your latest “tally” against someone and say it out loud in one sentence with a concrete suggestion of what to change.
Start your next reconciliation with a shared task and only then move on to talking.

chapters.h2: Family: freedom from home, endurance from the family line
chapters.conclusion: From home you may have brought lightness and freedom — or a habit of setting your own rhythm. Your family line gives you endurance but teaches you to cope alone, and that part of the inheritance is worth revising. The main task is to learn to ask for help and to create your own family rules consciously.

cards.label: Parents’ point
cards.caption: The Fool in the inner circle to the left of the centre — the atmosphere you grew up in: freedom, lightness, starting from a blank page.

cards.label: Children’s point
cards.caption: The Chariot between the large and the inner circle on the left — how you relate to children and younger people: to lead, develop, move forward.

formula.caption: **12 → 7 → 22.** The line of child–parent relationships: mask, children, parents. The atmosphere of the parental home affects both the attitude to children and how a person comes out into the world.

blocks: Most likely your home had a lot of freedom — or, on the contrary, freedom was the main question. The parents’ point describes the atmosphere a person grew up in and how the relationship between father and mother affected them, even if the parents were not around. Yours holds the Fool. In the plus it is a home where you could try, make mistakes and start again, where people knew how to forgive and did not hold on to the past. In the minus this energy has two opposites: irresponsible adults — or control over the people close to you and limits on their freedom.

Which version is yours, only you know. But both versions explain the Hanged Man’s mask. In a very free home a child sometimes learns to wait until one of the adults finally takes the situation in hand. In a home where freedom was limited, to wait until permitted. In both cases the pause becomes a way of living next to someone else’s element. You can check this hypothesis with one question: what did I get used to waiting for as a child — order or permission?

With younger people you are probably different: active and leading forward. The children’s point is the Chariot, the energy of movement and development: trips, sport, clubs, goals, a shared adventure. If you have children or will have them, their strength next to you is in doing things together. If you have no children, the same point speaks of junior colleagues, students, nieces and nephews. The minus of the seven is pressure and a race for results. The Fool in the parents’ point is a good antidote here: give the younger one the freedom to make mistakes that you may have had plenty of — or lacked.

blocks.h3: What the family line passes on

blocks: Your family line passes on endurance and at the same time a habit of coping alone. The strength of your family line is Strength (in detail — in the findings). Besides it, a line of three points runs from each corner of the scheme to the strength of the family line: the upper corners are the values of the family, its attitude to love, words, learning, laws; the lower ones are the deeds of the family, money, property, the body. Each line can be read both as a talent of the family and as its unfinished task.

There is a pattern in your lines. Both lines of values pass through the Lovers: in the family’s thoughts the main question is choice and love, and their plus and minus are confidence in your own choice and dependence on other people’s opinion. Both lines of deeds pass through the Hermit: in deeds the family relied on itself. The nine in its plus is self-sufficiency, wisdom and good personal boundaries; in its minus, withdrawal and mistrust. The result is a family formula: “the strong ones who cope alone”. The Hermit and Strength also stand in your total of all the chakras — in the physics and in the energy of the whole field.

Line by line it looks like this. From the male line of values — responsibility and the ability to sum things up; still to finish — choosing with your heart when the family expects the “right” decision. From the female line of values — endurance and lightness; still to finish — not measuring love by how much a person has put up with. From the male line of deeds — honesty and independence; still to finish — allowing yourself to be visible and not carrying everything alone. From the female line of deeds — faith in the future and the ability to get back up; still to finish — showing your talents. Where each of these lines arrives in your own scheme is told in the last finding: in money, in home, in partnership and in your centre.

The triples of both your female lines are analysed in one of the book’s examples, though on a different branch and in different areas. From her analysis only the general meaning of the energies applies here; the ready conclusion does not carry over to you.

In Lisovskaya’s book on tails, your karmic tail is placed among the tasks to do with family and kin: traditions, family rules, the link between generations. Her advice to people with such a tail is surprisingly simple: learn to ask your relatives for help, starting with small requests, invent new traditions and holidays, gather people around one table. For a person whose family strength stands on the point of pressure, this is hard advice: to ask means admitting you can’t manage alone. That is exactly why it is yours.

If there is no connection with your family, or it is a heavy one, the same advice works with other people. You can gather your own family from the people you have chosen, and you can start your own traditions from scratch.
actions: Ask one of your relatives for a small favour — advice, a recipe, a story from the past — and notice what you feel as you do.
Ask your elders how the family got through hard times: who was “the strong one”, who coped alone. Write down one phrase you want to keep for yourself and one you don’t want to pass on.
Invent one tradition of your own — a yearly dinner, a trip, a shared album — and give it a date.

chapters.h2: Karmic tail: where it sounds in your life
chapters.conclusion: The cards of your karmic tail stand in three more important places: in your earnings, in how you love and in what inspires you. So the tail’s old scenario is heard above all in money, in partnership and in the choice of work. At 35 the age point becomes the very card the tail ends with.

cards.label: Main point of the tail
cards.caption: The Hierophant in the large circle at the bottom is the karmic task; the whole tail is read from it.

cards.label: Middle of the tail
cards.caption: Judgement between the inner and the large circle at the bottom is a hint of what the task passes through.

blocks.h3: Where the tail sounds in your matrix

formula.caption: **15 → 20 → 5.** The tail runs from the inner circle below the centre to the large circle at the bottom. Its main point is the last one, the Hierophant: it sets the theme, and the other two hint at what the theme passes through.

blocks: The text above tells how such a tail works for everyone who has it. What is particular to you is where else its cards stand. Each of the three appears in another important role in your matrix, and that is where the tail sounds loudest.

ul: **The Hierophant — in money and in love.** It also stands in the middle of the money line, where earnings come from, in the physics of Anahata, that is, in how you show love, and in the planetary purpose. For you rules and traditions are at once a source of income and a way of loving: through faithfulness to your word and to rituals. So the question “how it should be done” comes up for you above all in money and in partnership.

**Judgement — in inspiration and in the second half of life.** It also stands in the upper left corner, the point of inspiration, and in the social purpose, which begins after forty. What lights you up — summing up, big transitions, recognition of what has been done — and where the tail hooks you — evaluation, your own or someone else’s — are one energy.

**The Devil — in understanding and in closeness.** The feelings of two chakras, Ajna and Anahata, are also the Devil in your matrix. When you are trying to understand something and when you love, the emotional charge is the same — the one the tail begins with. A strong “I want to know” and a strong “I want to be close” easily turn into a grip in you.

formula.caption: **20 = 20.** Judgement in the middle of the tail and in the upper left corner. The point of inspiration shows both what fills you and what drains you: in your case it is one energy — the evaluation of a result.

blocks: In this school the karmic tail itself is called a program — a combination of cards that carries a recurring task. In your case its links are also connected by a sum: three Hierophants, as the findings say, add up to the Devil, with which the tail begins. Our reading: that is why you can enter the old scenario from any side — through too many rules in money, through rituals in partnership, through a thirst for evaluation at work. And you can leave it from any side too.

The second program is trust on the talent line. Together with the tail it gives the main question of your maturity: whom and what to trust. Both answer in a similar way: trust what stands the test of action within a reasonable time.

blocks.h3: What to do about it in three areas

ul: **In money.** Before naming a price, ask yourself whose figure it is: yours — or the one it is “decent” to charge in your family and circle. The Hierophant in the point of earnings often brings someone else’s yardstick with it.

**In partnership.** Replace one inherited tradition — how you celebrate holidays, who does what at home, how you handle money — with one invented together. A rule you created yourselves does not switch the tail on.
**At work.** Note what inspired you this week: your own finished result or someone’s praise. The more of the first, the less power the second has.

blocks: From thirty-two and a half to thirty-five the age point of your scale is the Tower, the energy of tearing down the old and building the new. These are the years when you want to take apart outdated structures — agreements, roles, habits. The risk is taking apart what irritates you and keeping what has truly outlived itself.

At thirty-five the age point becomes the Hierophant — the card the tail ends with. The question “whose rules am I living by” stops being background and becomes the theme of several years. From thirty-seven and a half the point is Justice, your main talent. The order is a lucky one: first clear the ground, then choose your own rules, then check them for fairness.
actions: Before your next conversation about money, write down the figure you want to name and, next to it, where it came from: your own estimate or “that’s how it’s done”.
Pick one household tradition that was handed down to you and weighs on you, and suggest to the people close to you a version invented together.
Choose one thing you have long wanted to drop or take apart. Before taking it on, write down what will appear in its place.

chapters.h2: Body and rest: movement, people and silence on schedule
chapters.conclusion: You are filled up by movement, a change of scene, the warmth of people and finished stages. You are drained by the role of the strong one who can take anything, and by rest that turns into one more duty. The best format is active rest together with others plus short periods of silence that you set for yourself.

cards.label: Trigger
cards.caption: Strength in the upper right corner — endurance that easily turns into a habit of not resting.

cards.label: Dual
cards.caption: The Sun — warmth, light, joy you want to share.

blocks: You recover in motion and spend yourself on endurance. The matrix does not speak about health and makes no diagnoses; it suggests a rhythm that suits your character. If tiredness doesn’t go away even after rest, that is a reason to see a doctor.

**Movement.** The Chariot appears in your matrix three times, counting the calculated point, and the seven is charged with energy precisely in motion: a walk with a route, cycling, swimming, dancing, a weekend hike. This restores you faster than the sofa.

**A change of scene.** The Wheel in the centre loves a turn. The same weekends in the same place stop being restful after a month. Something small is enough: another park, a new route, a day trip to a nearby town.
**The warmth of people.** The Sun in the dual point and in the personal purpose asks for light: company, laughter, a shared celebration.

**A finished stage.** Judgement in the point of inspiration makes marking what you have done a form of rest too. A small ritual at the end of a project or a hard week — a dinner, a trip, simply a note of “what worked” — restores your strength better than jumping straight into the next task.

The main expense is Strength on the trigger point. In the minus of this energy is wearing yourself out and not knowing how to relax. It is easy for you to say “I can still go on”, and it is true — until the day you can’t. The second leak is the Hanged Man’s mask: in the minus of the twelfth energy are apathy and tiredness, and among its advice is to live for yourself too, not only for others. The third is the Hierophant, which stands in three of your points: rest by the rules (“at weekends one is supposed to…”) tires you even if it is formally correct.

blocks.h3: A contradiction worth taking into account

blocks: The Sun wants people and celebration. But the physics of the total of all your chakras is the Hermit, and it also stands in the middles of both material family lines: the body needs time alone. Rest where you are around people all the time wears you out by evening. Long solitude without people also soon stops being a joy. The solution is to combine them: a trip with friends where every day you have two hours for yourself; a party followed by a quiet evening already booked. Silence is better planned in advance, like a meeting, or someone else’s request will take it.

ul: Short active rest every week: two or three hours of movement outdoors with a clear route.
A change of scene every one or two months, at least for a weekend.
One treat for yourself a week — something just for pleasure, with no occasion and no use.
Rest in the calendar in advance, before you get tired. Strength doesn’t notice when it is time to stop, so the schedule makes the decision.
A small ritual after each finished stage.

blocks.h3: Signs that it is time to stop

blocks: A week has passed without a single walk. Rest has been cancelled for someone else’s business twice in a row. Any change of plans irritates you, though you usually love change — the Wheel is stuck. You want to drop everything and leave. Each of these signs is a reason to take a pause set by you, without waiting for tiredness to set it.
actions: Put four slots of active rest and two slots of silence for the coming month in your calendar — as meetings that cannot be moved.
Invent a ritual for the end of a stage and hold it after the next thing you finish.
Notice one of the signs of overload this week and on the same day take a pause, even for an hour.

chapters.h2: Chakras: where they repeat the main points of the matrix
chapters.conclusion: The most interesting thing about your chakras is the places where they repeat the main points of the matrix: calm in speech rests on the same card as the entry to money, the feeling after a job done on the card of inspiration, and love on the centre and the karmic task. The overall energy reserve of all the chakras is Strength, the same as in the strength of the family line and in the trigger point.
blocks: Seven chakras are seven floors of one life, from the body to meaning. First come the texts on each of them, then the links that can be seen only by comparing the chakras with other points of your scheme.

blocks.h3: A clear word and the entry to money are one card

formula.caption: **4 = 4.** The feeling in the chakra of speech and the entry of the money line are the Emperor.

blocks: Your money starts to move the moment the conversation about it takes shape. The feeling in Vishuddha, the chakra of speech, is the Emperor, and it also stands at the entry to money. In practice this means: until the amount, the deadline and the terms are said out loud, there is neither inner calm nor movement of money. Many people expect money to come first and calm to follow. For you it is the other way round: calm comes from something clearly said, and money follows it. So your shortest path to income runs through one uncomfortable sentence — naming the figure.

blocks.h3: The feeling after a job done is the card of inspiration

formula.caption: **20 = 20 = 20.** What you feel after an action, the point of inspiration and the purpose of the second half of life are Judgement.

blocks: What you feel after a job done is what inspires you. Manipura is will and action, and the feeling in it is Judgement for you. The same card stands in the upper left corner, the point of inspiration, and in the social purpose, which opens up after forty. The result is a chain: you act, you sum up, the result lights you up for the next step. And after forty the ability to sum things up becomes your role for others — gathering experience and passing it on.

A simple planning rule follows from this. Your tasks need visible finish points: stages, deliveries, interim results. Work with no finish leaves Manipura without fuel, and then your strength goes faster than the amount of work would suggest. The risk of the same link is judging yourself after every step. A result is needed to light you up; a verdict on yourself puts the fire out.

blocks.h3: Love stands on the centre and on the karmic task

blocks: In love two cards meet in your matrix that meet like this nowhere else among the chakras. The energy of Anahata is the Wheel, the same card as in your centre. And how love shows itself is the Hierophant, your karmic task and point of earnings. To love, for you, means staying yourself in motion while keeping agreements. Hence a practical conclusion: rules in a couple are the same growth zone for you as in money. Overdo the rules and you will meet in love the same control and protest the finding about the three Hierophants talks about. Keep the measure and you will get a reliability many people lack.

The energy in the total of all seven chakras is Strength; a coincidence with the strength of the family line occurs for about one date in thirteen, and in your case the trigger point adds to them. Your whole energy reserve rests on endurance, and it matters to spend that reserve on your own things, not on putting up with things. The physics of the total is the Hermit: the body needs its own time alone — more on this in the chapter on rest.
actions: In your next money conversation name the amount and the deadline in the very first sentence and notice what happens to your calm.
Break your longest task into stages with a visible finish and mark the first of them.
Pick one rule in your relationship that holds only because you insist on it, and discuss it afresh.

chapters.h2: Your sign in the Tarot: the lion, the sun and fire
chapters.conclusion: By the Golden Dawn correspondences your sign, Leo, is the Strength card, its ruler the Sun is the Sun card, and its element, fire, is the Judgement card. All three stand in prominent places in your matrix. This is a different system, not the matrix method, but it highlights the same theme: endurance that matters not to turn into endless patience.

cards.label: Card of the sign
cards.caption: Strength is Leo’s card by the Golden Dawn correspondences; in your matrix it stands in the upper right corner, on the trigger point.

blocks: By a neighbouring system, the three cards of your sign stand exactly where the main theme of your matrix runs. The link between Tarot cards and zodiac signs was not invented in the Destiny Matrix: it is the system of the English Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn of the late nineteenth century, described, for example, by Benebell Wen in her book “Holistic Tarot”. The matrix is calculated from the date differently and does not use signs, so everything below is a view from a neighbouring tradition.

**Sign — Leo, card — Strength.** You were born on 12 August, and Wen writes that the Strength card can refer to the sign of Leo and the period from 23 July to 22 August. In your matrix Strength stands in the upper right corner — on the trigger point, where you are easiest to pressure — and in the strength of the family line. So the card of your sign in one system is your support and your vulnerable spot in another. In Waite’s picture on this card a woman holds a lion with a chain of flowers; for Wen, Strength upright is the victory of gentleness and compassion. Leo’s fire works better in you when it is held gently.

**Ruler — the Sun, card — the Sun.** In your matrix the Sun stands at the crossing of the lines of money and relationships and in the personal purpose. Wen writes of the Sun card as success that gets noticed, and also as release from previous exhausting toil. For a person with Strength on the trigger this is a precise landmark: shine rather than haul.

**Element — fire, card — Judgement.** In the Golden Dawn system fire corresponds to Judgement. In your matrix Judgement stands in the upper left corner, the point of inspiration, in the middle of the karmic tail and in the social purpose. To be honest: Wen mentions two schools — one assigns Judgement to fire, the other to water — and she herself chooses water. We take the classic Golden Dawn correspondence.

If you put the three cards together, you get a picture familiar from the chapters above. The fire of your sign holds you and tests your strength in one place, warms others and you yourself in another, and lights you up and judges in a third. The main lesson of this picture: Leo’s fire is there to shine and inspire. If it goes into silent endurance, it goes out fastest.
actions: Remember the last time you “shone” — spoke in public, shared, rejoiced openly. Plan something similar for the coming month.
Next time you are asked to take on more, remember the chain of flowers in Waite’s picture: holding gently is strength too.

chapters.h2: For the people close to you: a short guide
chapters.conclusion: This chapter can be shown to a partner, a friend or family. In short: she sees unfairness at once but doesn’t speak about it at once; she is inspired by honesty, movement and recognition; it is better to make peace with her through action, and to agree on things in advance and out loud; in closeness she wants strength of feeling and freedom.
blocks: This chapter is written for those around her. If you are reading it about someone close to you, here is the main thing about how she is made and what makes things easier with her.

ul: Honesty. Say it straight, even if it is unpleasant: she respects the truth more than convenience.
Movement. Suggest going somewhere, starting, doing something together — a new project or route charges her up more than a present.
Recognition of her conclusion. When she has untangled and explained something, tell her it helped. Her talent is precision, and it matters to her that the precision was noticed.
Summing up. Mark a finished stage together: a move, a project, a hard year. For her it is a celebration.
“You’re strong, you’ll manage.” This is her vulnerable spot: she will manage, but she will remember that her strength was used.
Double standards. A rule that applies to her and not to you hurts more than a rude word.
Lecturing. If you explain to her “how it’s done” without her asking, she will either shut down or do the opposite.
Promises not kept. She notes each one — even if out loud she says “never mind”.
In advance and concretely: who does what, how much it costs, by what date. A clear frame calms her.
Out loud. She hears hints, but she will weigh them rather than act on them.
By explaining why. A rule with an explanation she will accept; a rule “because that’s how it has to be”, hardly.
By leaving her the right to her own conclusion. Give her time to think — but ask when she will be ready to answer.
First a shared task, then talk. A walk together, cooking, a trip ease the tension faster than a long analysis.
Name what you were wrong about, concretely: what, when, what you will do differently. A vague “sorry if anything” won’t convince her.
Don’t rush her. If she said “I need to think until this evening”, that is an honest deadline.

If she has withdrawn into herself, don’t bombard her with questions. Suggest doing something together — a walk, a drive, cooking dinner. In motion she will tell you sooner than sitting across the table.
Give her the part of the work where things need to be checked, compared and concluded: there she is stronger than most.
Name the criteria in advance. The task “do it well” torments her; the task “here are three signs it’s ready” pleases her.
Don’t change the rules silently. If something has changed, explain why — otherwise she will consider it unfair, even if she says nothing.
Give her pause a deadline: “Think it over until Thursday.” Without a deadline she will weigh things for a long time; with one she will come back with a ready and precise answer.
Don’t load her with someone else’s area just because she won’t refuse. She won’t refuse, but her trust in you will shrink.

blocks: She loves seriously and strongly: warm but limp relationships bore her. She needs intensity of feeling and at the same time her own freedom — checking up on her and jealousy put her out faster than distance. On the outside she looks calm, so her opinion is easy to miss in a general conversation: ask her directly what she thinks — the answer usually turns out to be the most precise of the evening. Her outward calm doesn’t mean she doesn’t care; usually it means she is still weighing things up.

People who shine themselves do well next to her: those who have their own work, humour and warmth and are not afraid of being seen as imperfect. She is at ease with people who don’t turn every failure into a disaster. And one more thing: she rarely asks for help first. If you see that she is once again carrying everything herself, offer something concrete — “I’ll take care of dinners this week” — instead of a general “just say if you need anything”. A general offer she will politely decline; a concrete one she is more likely to accept.
